## Problem
The scheduled main `test.yml` `sweep (windows)` job failed on three consecutive scheduled runs (34321330218, 34353500045, 34391071987; 2026-09-08..09). The failure signature is a collection-time `ModuleNotFoundError` from `tests/interfaces/store/test_mcp_write_lock_dead_stamp.py`, followed by setup-error cascades in store/MCP round-trip tests. Ubuntu gating and macOS sweep pass on the same SHAs, so this is Windows-specific.

## Suspected root cause
`tests/interfaces/store/test_mcp_write_lock_dead_stamp.py` imports the POSIX-only `fcntl` module at module import time. Windows has no `fcntl`, so pytest fails during collection before test-level setup or skip logic can run. The production lock abstraction already supports both POSIX and Windows (`src/rebar/_store/lock_kernel.py`); the red sweep appears to be a test portability bug in a POSIX-specific regression test for reclaiming a stale mkdir owner stamp after acquiring the fcntl leg.

## Plan
1. Confirm the Windows log points at `import fcntl` in `tests/interfaces/store/test_mcp_write_lock_dead_stamp.py` and inspect the production lock abstraction for the existing portable/Windows path.
2. Add a module-level Windows collection guard for this POSIX-only test module, or otherwise move the `fcntl` import behind a POSIX-only skip so Windows can collect the suite.
3. Keep the fix scoped to test portability; do not change production locking semantics unless investigation proves the production abstraction is faulty.
4. Validate with the smallest local tests that can cover the changed module and static collection behavior, then run the repo verification command. Because Windows cannot be run locally, use a manually dispatched or Gerrit CI Windows sweep if available and rely on CI evidence for the final Windows proof.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The root cause is identified from the Windows CI log and recorded in the ticket: collection fails because the POSIX-only `fcntl` import is evaluated on Windows before any guard can skip the module.
- [ ] The offending test module or fixture is portable at collection time on Windows; if skipped, the skip is scoped only to the POSIX-only fcntl behavior and explains why the production cross-platform lock path is covered elsewhere.
- [ ] No production lock behavior is weakened for POSIX or Windows.
- [ ] Local targeted validation passes for the changed test module and relevant lock-kernel tests on this host.
- [ ] `env -u GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL -u GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM -u GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make verify PYTEST_WORKERS=2` passes before push, or any local baseline/environment failure is classified and Gerrit `Verified +1` supplies the gating verdict.
- [ ] Gerrit CI reports `Verified +1`; if a Windows sweep/manual dispatch is available for the submitted patchset or merged main, record its run id and result before closing.

## Testing / Verification
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest -q tests/interfaces/store/test_mcp_write_lock_dead_stamp.py tests/unit/test_lock_kernel.py` from the fresh worktree.
- `env -u GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL -u GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM -u GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make verify PYTEST_WORKERS=2` before push.
- Gerrit CI `Verified +1` before submit.
- Windows sweep/manual workflow evidence when available; otherwise static proof plus Gerrit verification is recorded honestly.

## File impact
`tests/interfaces/store/test_mcp_write_lock_dead_stamp.py` — collection-time guard for a POSIX-only fcntl regression test.
